feature: RFC8785 plain zero baseline alongside the string form, control for the negzero case (distinct canonical preimage)
input_note: input.json stores the original wire JSON text as bytes (UTF-8, no BOM, single trailing LF). The trailing LF is not part of any signing preimage; only the canonical JSON bytes listed below are signed.

n.note: Numeric member. RFC 8785 serializes the number zero without a sign, so the canonical token is 0 with no leading minus (the integer -0 token canonicalises to 0).

s.note: String member carried as a separate member to distinguish a numeric value from its string form. RFC 8785 serializes JSON strings verbatim (with quotes, after the RFC 8785 string escaping rules); the content is never numerically normalized, so "0" stays a quoted string and must not become the number 0 or lose its minus sign.

member_order_note: RFC 8785 serializes object members in lexicographic key order; "n" precedes "s".

rejected_literal.description: Preimage of a literal-preserving canonicalizer that keeps the integer -0 token instead of emitting 0. For the negzero case it is byte-identical to the raw wire text (input.json minus its trailing LF): the non-conformant implementation signs the wire literal as if it were the canonical form.

confusions.label: string-member-coerced-to-number
confusions.description: Preimage of a canonicalizer that treats the string member as a number: the quotes are dropped and "s" is serialised as 0. A numeric value is conflated with its string form.

distinct_from_case.note: negzero signs {"n":0,"s":"-0"}; its canonical preimage and signature.sig are different bytes from this case.

note: Control case. A leading plus sign ('+0') is not a legal JSON number token (RFC 8259 grammar), so no +0 input fixture is provided. The plain integer 0 / string "0" document has its own canonical preimage and its own signature.sig, which differ from the negzero case because the string member is preserved verbatim ("0" vs "-0"). The rejected-literal and types-swapped-confusion bytes live in ../negzero/ and are cross-pinned here by hex.
checker_assertions: raw wire text carries separate numeric member n (token 0) and string member s (token "0")
per-member canonical forms: "n":0 (number) and "s":"0" (string, quoted verbatim)
Ed25519 verify(pubkey, signature.sig, rejected literal {"n":-0,"s":"-0"}) == INVALID
Ed25519 verify(pubkey, signature.sig, ../negzero confusion types-swapped) == INVALID
